[head=2][color=#e8b04b]Custom Controls and Combat Basics[/color][/head]
This page covers controls that differ from, or are especially important to, standard Space Station 14. For movement, inventory, interaction, and interface basics, start with [textlink="Controls" link="Controls"]. You can rebind controls here:
[head=3][color=#e8b04b]Melee Combat[/color][/head] Melee uses a detailed system with slashing, parrying and executions.
- Turn on [bold]Combat Mode[/bold] from your action bar before trying to attack or parry. - [color=#6ab7d6][keybind="Use"/][/color] performs a committed melee attack that sweeps a wide arc and hits everyone in it. - [color=#6ab7d6][keybind="UseSecondary"/][/color] parries or blocks an incoming attack. Good timing gives you a major advantage. - [color=#6ab7d6][keybind="MouseMiddle"/][/color] performs a lighter attack on a single target, on a longer cooldown than the wide swing. Use it when an ally is standing next to your target.
For parry timing, stamina, and executions, see [textlink="Melee Combat" link="MeleeCombat"].
[head=3][color=#e8b04b]Looking Ahead / Peeking[/color][/head] Hold [color=#6ab7d6][keybind="LookUp"/][/color] and your camera slides toward the direction you are facing, letting you see [color=#e8b04b]further than normal[/color].
Use it to look around a corner or wall, spot a threat approaching from far away, or see your target before you shoot. If you want to check where you are aiming before firing, this key is a lifesaver.
[head=3][color=#e8b04b]Racking / Chambering Your Weapon[/color][/head] Most firearms here [color=#d9776c]do not chamber themselves automatically[/color]. Even with a magazine loaded, the gun will not fire if there is no round in the chamber.
Most long guns must first be wielded with a free hand. Press [color=#6ab7d6][keybind="ActivateItemInHand"/][/color] to wield the weapon, then activate it again to rack it and feed a round into the chamber.
Keep in mind: - Rack the weapon once when you first pick it up. - After a magazine runs dry, load a fresh one and rack again. - Pump-action and manual weapons may need to be cycled after every shot.
To remove a chambered round, put the weapon in one hand, make the other hand active and empty, then use [color=#6ab7d6][keybind="AltActivateItemInWorld"/][/color] on the weapon.
[head=3][color=#e8b04b]Wielding (Two Hands)[/color][/head] Many rifles, shotguns and heavy weapons [color=#d9776c]cannot be used properly one-handed[/color]. To wield a weapon, press [color=#6ab7d6][keybind="ActivateItemInHand"/][/color] while holding it and keeping your other hand free.
Pressing [color=#6ab7d6][keybind="ActivateItemInHand"/][/color] again while wielded will rack and chamber most firearms.
Wielding improves accuracy a lot, and some weapons can only be fired while wielded. You need a free hand to wield.
[head=3][color=#e8b04b]Lying Down and Taking Cover[/color][/head] [color=#6ab7d6][keybind="ToggleStanding"/][/color] makes you lie down or stand back up.
While lying down, press [color=#6ab7d6][keybind="ToggleCrawlingUnder"/][/color] to hide under or behind certain objects. This helps you take cover and stay out of sight.
Lying down also makes you a smaller target and lets you use low cover more effectively.
[head=3][color=#e8b04b]Action Slots[/color][/head] You can trigger abilities on the action bar with the number keys shown on their slots. By default, the top-row keys [color=#6ab7d6][keybind="Hotbar1"/][/color] through [color=#6ab7d6][keybind="Hotbar0"/][/color] activate the corresponding slots.
This is much faster than clicking your actions.
Drag and drop actions to arrange them. [color=#d9776c]Numpad 0 does not activate an action[/color]; it opens the Guidebook.
[head=3][color=#e8b04b]Other Important Keys[/color][/head] - [color=#6ab7d6][keybind="SwapHands"/][/color] swaps your active hand, letting you quickly switch between your weapon and another item. - [color=#6ab7d6][keybind="ActivateItemInWorld"/][/color] uses or interacts with something in the world, such as doors, crates, and hatches. - [color=#6ab7d6][keybind="Drop"/][/color] drops the item in your hand. - [color=#6ab7d6][keybind="ThrowItemInHand"/][/color] throws the item in your hand. - [color=#6ab7d6][keybind="ExamineEntity"/][/color] examines something, which is always useful for learning what it is and how it is used.
